groups.name: definition
groups.asks: Does this episode count as serendipity?

codes.label: Already searching
codes.when: The account shows a search or effort under way at the time.
codes.example: 'I'd been trying ideas for months when...'
codes.notwhen: The founder was not looking for anything at the time; leave this code off.

codes.label: Agency: acted on it
codes.when: The founder describes their own response to the event and links the result to it.
codes.example: 'I wrote back that night and offered to build it.'
codes.notwhen: The benefit simply arrived with no action by the founder; code rival-01 (pure luck) instead.

codes.label: Surprise
codes.when: The founder says an event, contact, result or reaction was unexpected or not part of the plan.
codes.example: 'I never expected anyone to ask for that.'
codes.notwhen: The founder got what they planned and expected, on schedule.

codes.label: Value
codes.when: The founder presents what followed as useful or important for them or the venture.
codes.example: 'That one email became our biggest customer.'
codes.notwhen: Nothing of value came of it; code outcome-25 instead.

groups.name: type
groups.asks: What kind of serendipity is it?

codes.label: Mertonian: sought, found unexpectedly
codes.when: A known problem or need was solved by something that turned up unexpectedly.
codes.example: 'We needed a supplier, and the guy next to me on the plane ran one.'
codes.notwhen: The find answered a different problem or changed the goal; use type-02.

codes.label: Walpolian: sought one, found another
codes.when: A project or search ended up producing a different product, market or direction.
codes.example: 'We were building a tool for agencies and schools started buying it.'
codes.notwhen: The original goal was met unexpectedly (type-01), or there was no search (type-03).

codes.label: Not looking at all
codes.when: The founder stumbled on the idea, often solving their own or a friend's problem, before planning a business.
codes.example: 'I made it for myself, then people kept asking for one.'
codes.notwhen: The founder already wanted a business (type-04) or pursued a specific goal (type-01, type-02).

codes.label: Wanted a business, any business
codes.when: The founder was open to any opportunity when one turned up.
codes.example: 'I knew I wanted to work for myself; then a friend mentioned...'
codes.notwhen: No wish to found (type-03), or already pursuing a specific idea (type-01, type-02).

codes.label: Bushian: exploring, met existing need
codes.when: The founder was trying things out or browsing, and found the answer to a need they already had.
codes.example: 'I was playing with a new tool and realised it fixed our shipping problem.'
codes.notwhen: The founder was searching for that answer (type-01), or the need only appeared later (type-06).

codes.label: Stephanian: solution first, problem later
codes.when: The founder describes a find, skill or product that sat unused until a need turned up.
codes.example: 'We had built that feature years ago; only when customers asked did we see what it was for.'
codes.notwhen: Problem and solution came together (type-03), or the find met an existing need (type-05).

anomaly.when: The episode is serendipity, but no type code describes it
anomaly.notwhen: A type fits roughly: use it and note the doubt

groups.name: rival
groups.asks: What else could explain the same story?

codes.label: Pure luck, no action
codes.when: The founder presents an event as a windfall that simply happened.
codes.example: 'A big blog wrote about us out of nowhere and sales took off.'
codes.notwhen: The founder also noticed and acted on the event; then consider serendipity instead.

codes.label: Systematic search
codes.when: The founder decided what to look for and found it as expected.
codes.example: 'I analysed 40 niches and picked the one with the best margins.'
codes.notwhen: The search was under way but the answer came unexpectedly (definition-04).

codes.label: A plan carried out
codes.when: The founder describes following a plan made in advance, step by step, without unexpected turns.
codes.example: 'We had a five-year plan and stuck to it.'
codes.notwhen: The point is how the idea was searched for; use rival-06.

codes.label: Working with what's at hand
codes.when: The founder describes building from their own means, making do and recombining, and reports no surprise.
codes.example: 'I had a van and some carpentry skills, so I started there.'
codes.notwhen: An unexpected event and its recognition are also present; then it supports serendipity.

anomaly.when: The account fits another explanation that is not a rival code
anomaly.notwhen: The founder only denies chance: that is account

groups.name: trigger
groups.sq: Where does it happen, and what sets it off?

codes.label: Something odd was noticed
codes.when: The founder saw an odd result, behaviour or detail and looked into it instead of ignoring it.
codes.example: 'Customers kept using it for something we never designed it for.'
codes.notwhen: The surprise came from the market as a whole (trigger-24) or a mistake (trigger-04).

codes.label: A mistake or accident
codes.when: The founder traces the idea or path to a mistake or mishap.
codes.example: 'We ordered the wrong size by accident and it sold better.'
codes.notwhen: A planned attempt simply failed and was reused elsewhere; if nothing fits, MIS-TRG.

codes.label: A chance meeting
codes.when: The founder describes meeting someone by chance: at an event, through a seat on a plane, a shared office.
codes.example: 'I met my co-founder at a wedding.'
codes.notwhen: What mattered was a passing remark (trigger-17), or the meeting was arranged.

codes.label: A passing remark
codes.when: The founder says an offhand remark sparked the idea or changed direction.
codes.example: 'My sister said, "you should sell these".'
codes.notwhen: The person made a concrete offer or request (trigger-18), or the relationship mattered (trigger-14).

codes.label: An unasked-for offer or request
codes.when: The founder received an unexpected message, contract, partnership proposal or product request and acted on it.
codes.example: 'A hotel emailed asking if we could make 500.'
codes.notwhen: Someone only mentioned a need in passing (trigger-17), or many customers showed a pattern (trigger-24).

codes.label: An unexpected market signal
codes.when: The founder describes a demand spike, a surprising best-seller, or users doing something unforeseen, which pointed to a new path.
codes.example: 'One product we added as an extra outsold everything else.'
codes.notwhen: One customer asked directly (trigger-18), or the surprise was technical; if nothing fits, MIS-TRG.

anomaly.when: Something unexpected started it, but no trigger code names that kind of event
anomaly.notwhen: The trigger is unclear: leave trigger blank

groups.name: background
groups.asks: What did the founder already have?
groups.sq: What do founders bring and do?

codes.label: Relevant expertise
codes.when: The founder credits their professional or industry knowledge for recognising the opportunity.
codes.example: 'After ten years in logistics, I knew straight away what that meant.'
codes.notwhen: What mattered was a specific problem they were already working on (background-02).

codes.label: A problem already in mind
codes.when: The founder says they were already wrestling with a particular problem when the input arrived.
codes.example: 'I'd been trying to fix my own sleep for years.'
codes.notwhen: The founder credits general expertise without a specific problem (background-01).

codes.label: Idea grew from their work
codes.when: The idea is traced to the founder's current or past work, projects or role.
codes.example: 'As a nurse, I saw the same problem every shift.'
codes.notwhen: The founder credits expertise in general without tying it to a role or activity (background-01).

codes.label: Their network brought it
codes.when: An opportunity or referral came through the founder's contacts.
codes.example: 'An old colleague passed my name to a buyer.'
codes.notwhen: The founder met someone new by chance (trigger-14), not through existing contacts.

anomaly.when: The founder brought something relevant that no background code covers
anomaly.notwhen: It is a circumstance, not something the founder had: that is condition

groups.name: mechanism
groups.asks: What did the founder do to turn it into something?
groups.sq: What do founders bring and do?

codes.label: Noticing it
codes.when: The founder describes the moment they registered a cue and kept it in mind.
codes.example: 'Everyone laughed it off, but I couldn't stop thinking about it.'
codes.notwhen: The founder goes on to link it to a need or use (mechanism-06).

codes.label: Connecting the dots
codes.when: The founder describes realising how the new information fit something they knew or needed.
codes.example: 'I put the two together and thought, this could be a product.'
codes.notwhen: The founder only noticed the cue without linking it (mechanism-02).

codes.label: Acting on it
codes.when: The founder describes what they did next and how quickly.
codes.example: 'I built a landing page that weekend.'
codes.notwhen: Acting meant dropping or changing the original plan (mechanism-23).

codes.label: Changing the plan
codes.when: The founder describes abandoning or changing their idea or strategy because of the event.
codes.example: 'We scrapped the app and focused on the API.'
codes.notwhen: The founder acted on it without changing any plan (mechanism-22).

codes.label: Following what took off
codes.when: The founder describes small tests, early customer feedback or usage data, and backing the surprise winner.
codes.example: 'We ran a few ads, one took off, so we went all in on that.'
codes.notwhen: The experiments were on materials or the product, not customers; if nothing fits, MIS-MEC.

anomaly.when: The founder did something with the event that no mechanism code covers

groups.name: role
groups.asks: What part did it play in the venture?
groups.sq: What does it change in the venture?

codes.label: Started the venture
codes.when: The founder traces the origin of the business to the event.
codes.example: 'That conversation is why the company exists.'
codes.notwhen: The founder never meant to found (role-02), or an existing venture changed course (role-08).

codes.label: Accidental founder
codes.when: The founder stresses they were not trying to be an entrepreneur.
codes.example: 'I never meant to start a company; it just grew.'
codes.notwhen: The founder already wanted to start something and found the idea by chance (role-01).

codes.label: Changed the venture's direction
codes.when: The founder describes a clear turning point away from the original plan.
codes.example: 'After that, we stopped selling to consumers and went B2B.'
codes.notwhen: Small tweaks with the same purpose, or growth along the same path (role-16).

codes.label: Moved the venture forward
codes.when: The founder credits a chance event with a jump in growth or progress.
codes.example: 'Getting on that podcast doubled our sales.'
codes.notwhen: The event changed what the venture does (role-08).

anomaly.when: It played a part in the venture other than starting, redirecting or advancing it

groups.name: outcome
groups.sq: What does it change in the venture?

codes.label: A new product or service
codes.when: The founder traces something they now sell or do back to the event.
codes.example: 'That's how our best-selling kit was born.'
codes.notwhen: What came out was a new market or customers, not a new offering (outcome-03).

codes.label: A new market or opportunity
codes.when: The founder says the event opened their eyes to customers or channels they had not targeted.
codes.example: 'We realised dentists were our real market.'
codes.notwhen: The result was a new product or service (outcome-01).

codes.label: Growth and results
codes.when: The founder links business results to the event.
codes.example: 'That channel is now 60% of our revenue.'
codes.notwhen: The founder describes no measurable or stated result; use only outcome-01 or outcome-03 as fits.

codes.label: Nothing came of it
codes.when: The founder recounts a chance signal or contact they ignored or did not follow up, sometimes with regret.
codes.example: 'Someone offered to invest early on and I said no.'
codes.notwhen: The find was pursued and led somewhere; use the outcome codes for that.

anomaly.when: A result that no outcome code covers

groups.name: condition
groups.asks: What made it easier or harder?
groups.sq: When is it more or less likely?

codes.label: Putting themselves in chance's way
codes.when: The founder describes deliberate habits that invite chance.
codes.example: 'I said yes to every coffee meeting that first year.'
codes.notwhen: The founder only says they are open to luck, without describing actions.

codes.label: Cheap to try
codes.when: The founder says they could test it quickly and cheaply, or had a safety net.
codes.example: 'It cost me $50 to see if anyone would buy it.'
codes.notwhen: The point is lacking money to follow up (condition-35 or MIS-CND).

codes.label: Loose plans
codes.when: The founder describes having no fixed plan, moving step by step, or being locked into a plan.
codes.example: 'We never had a business plan, so it was easy to switch.'
codes.notwhen: The constraint was obligations to investors or contracts; if no core code fits, use MIS-CND.

codes.label: Little money or resources
codes.when: Being short of money or resources led the founder to improvise or take an unexpected opportunity.
codes.example: 'We couldn't afford ads, so we said yes to any partnership.'
codes.notwhen: Lack of money stopped them following up; if no core code fits, use MIS-CND.

anomaly.when: A circumstance that made it easier or harder, not covered by a condition code

groups.name: account
groups.asks: How does the founder tell it afterwards?

codes.label: Told as if planned
codes.when: The story is told as linear or intended, while the details show unplanned turns.
codes.example: 'We always knew this was the market', though earlier they describe stumbling into it.
codes.notwhen: The founder credits skill rather than recasting the sequence; if nothing fits, MIS-ACC.

codes.label: Credited to luck
codes.when: The founder uses luck language.
codes.example: 'Honestly, we just got lucky.'
codes.notwhen: The founder divides credit between luck and their own effort (account-09).

codes.label: Part luck, part effort
codes.when: The founder says success was partly luck and partly effort, or that they made their own luck.
codes.example: 'Luck opened the door, but we worked hard to walk through it.'
codes.notwhen: The founder credits luck alone (account-08).

codes.label: Only clear in hindsight
codes.when: The founder describes something that seemed small or unimportant then but crucial now.
codes.example: 'I almost didn't go to that meetup.'
codes.notwhen: A setback first seen as bad luck was reinterpreted; if nothing fits, MIS-ACC.

anomaly.when: A way of telling it that no account code covers

new.when: Relevant to the research question, but no group asks about it
new.notwhen: It belongs to a group: use that group's anomaly code
